title: Fix VPC endpoints apply race (explicit depends_on) + add regression coverage
author: Sahana Iyer
description:
Context: We’ve had intermittent failures in the CI integration apply test (and one pilot rerun) where interface endpoints are created before their dependent route tables / subnet associations / security group rules are fully materialized. The AWS API is eventually consistent here and Terraform can schedule the endpoint creates earlier than we expect when the dependency graph is only implicit through references. Symptoms: `InvalidSubnetID.NotFound`, `InvalidGroup.NotFound`, or `VpcEndpointIdNotFound` during endpoint association, usually resolved by a second apply. This PR makes the dependency ordering explicit in `modules/vpc-endpoints` and adds a regression test that reproduces the original failure mode (endpoint creation happening in parallel with SG/RT changes).

Changes: 1) Add explicit `depends_on` for `aws_vpc_endpoint` resources to ensure route table associations and endpoint SG rules are applied before endpoint create/association. 2) Tighten module inputs so the dependency edges are available even when using "existing VPC" partial adoption mode (subnet IDs passed in). 3) Add an integration test scenario that intentionally forces ordering pressure (plan/apply with parallelism > 1) and asserts no endpoint association errors. 4) Update docs note in the integration test harness about why we rely on explicit `depends_on` for endpoints.

Notes: This is intentionally small and targeted. It does not change which endpoints we create or the default endpoint set; only ordering + test coverage. No breaking input changes.

Verification: - `terraform fmt` / `validate` - `tflint` / `checkov` - Integration apply matrix (us-east-1 + us-west-2; NAT=single and NAT=per-az) - Reproduced failure on current main by forcing parallelism, confirmed this PR eliminates the flake across 20 runs.

Follow-ups: We should consider adding `-parallelism=1` as a last-resort escape hatch in the harness, but prefer keeping parallelism and fixing the graph. Also adding a short troubleshooting entry in the Quickstart doc once this merges.
commits: vpc-endpoints: add explicit depends_on for interface endpoint resources
vpc-endpoints: ensure sg/rt dependency edges exist in existing-vpc mode
integration-tests: add regression scenario for endpoint create/association ordering
docs: annotate harness with endpoint ordering rationale
conversation:
Victor Alvarez (review): Can you clarify what the missing edge was? I see SG IDs referenced by the endpoint, so I’d expect Terraform to order correctly.

Sahana Iyer (author): The endpoint references the SG ID, yes, but the failure we saw wasn’t SG create vs endpoint create; it was SG rule propagation + subnet/rt association propagation. In the existing-vpc mode we don’t always have direct references from endpoint resources to the route table association resources, so Terraform can schedule endpoint creation while RT association resources are still in-flight. Also, AWS will sometimes accept the SG ID but then fail the endpoint association if the rule changes haven’t propagated. Adding explicit `depends_on` for `aws_route_table_association.*` and the SG rule resources makes the ordering deterministic.

Irene Choi (review): +1 on determinism. Please make sure we’re not over-scoping the dependency and slowing down applies unnecessarily.

Sahana Iyer (author): Agree. I kept it narrow: only interface endpoints depend on (a) endpoint security group rules and (b) route table association resources when we’re managing them. Gateway endpoints (S3) stay as-is.

Benji Okafor (review): Does this affect the stable outputs contract consumed by the installer?

Sahana Iyer (author): No output shape changes. Endpoint IDs and DNS entries remain identical. Only ordering + additional test module.

Kevin Osei (security review): Any changes to endpoint policy stubs or private DNS behavior?

Sahana Iyer (author): None. No policy changes. Private DNS toggles unchanged.

Victor Alvarez (request changes): Can you add a comment near the `depends_on` explaining the eventual consistency / SUP-2204 context so someone doesn’t remove it later?

Sahana Iyer (author): Done in `modules/vpc-endpoints/main.tf` above the interface endpoint resources. Also linked SUP-2204 and ENG-4825.

Victor Alvarez (approval): Looks good. Regression test is a nice addition.

Irene Choi (approval): Approved.

Benji Okafor (approval): Approved.

Kevin Osei (approval): Approved from security side (no behavior change).
